1972 Constitution: ‘Repealing it is like denying Liberation War’
2025-01-14T04:00:00+06:00 | STAFF CORRESPONDENT
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/1972-constitution-repealing-it-denying-liberation-war-3798946

Thirty-six decorated freedom fighters have condemned and protested the attempt to repeal the 1972 constitution, saying that the issues achieved and resolved through the Liberation War cannot be questioned or changed.

In a joint media statement issued yesterday, they also condemned and protested the incidents of assaulting and humiliating the freedom fighters, vandalising their homes and offices of the Muktijoddha Sangsad across the country since August 5.

The gallantry award recipient freedom fighters said amending or updating the constitution to meet the aspirations of the people as per the need of the time is an ongoing process, but repealing the 1972 constitution achieved through the great Liberation War means denying the Liberation War and betraying the three million martyrs.

In the more than half a century since Bangladesh's independence, the previous governments have repeatedly distorted the original constitution of 1972 in their own ways to achieve their interests, thus going against the original spirit of the Liberation War, they said.

In the statement, the freedom fighters said, "The constitution of 1972 cannot be repealed under any circumstances, but rather we strongly demand from the current interim government that the original constitution of 1972 be reinstated in its entirety."

The statement was signed by the Titled Freedom Fighters Association Secretary General Md Shahjahan Kabir (Bir Pratik).

Other signatories include AW Chowdhury Bir Uttam and Bir Pratik, Captain (retd) Shahab Uddin (Bir Uttam), Major (retd) ATM Hamidul Hossain (Bir Bikram), Lt Col (retd) Abdur Rouf (Bir Bikram), Honorary Captain (retd) Abdul Haque Bir Bikram, Abul Kalam Azad (Bir Bikram), Maj Gen (retd) Md. Masudur Rahman Bir Pratik, Captain Kazi A Sattar Bir Pratik, DIG (retd) Kazi Joynal Abedin Bir Pratik, Md Momin Ullah Patwari Bir Pratik and Anwar Hossain Pahari Bir Pratik.

The other freedom fighters who signed the letter are Mizanur Rahman Khan Bir Pratik, Mozammel Haque Mahbub Elahi Ranju, Nur Uddin, Mohiuddin Manik, Bahar Uddin Reza, Professor Abdullah Al Mamun, Delwar Hossain, Ratan Ali Sharif, Syed Rezwan Ali, Rafiqul Islam, Golam Azad, Md Idris Ali, Anwar Hossain, Anisur Rahman, Maj (retd) Waqar Hasan, Sardar Mohsin Ali, A Hakim, Bazlur Mahmud, Nurul Haque, Nurul Islam, Habibur Rahman, Fazlul Haque, Abdullah and Abdul Gafur.
